verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {applicant_name}, the Applicant herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to my personal knowledge. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Applicant

promptInstructions: Draft an application for amendment of pleadings under Order 6 Rule 17 read with Section 151 CPC.

Order 6 R.17 has TWO parts: (i) Main provision — court may at any stage allow amendments necessary to determine real questions in controversy. (ii) Proviso (added 2002) — no application for amendment shall be allowed after trial has commenced, unless court concludes that despite due diligence, party could not have raised the matter before commencement of trial.
Pre-trial: liberal approach. Post-trial: strict due diligence test.
Cite Salem Advocate Bar Association v. Union of India (2005) 6 SCC 344 — proviso constitutional; due diligence test affirmed.

Cite Revajeetu Builders & Developers v. Narayanaswamy & Sons (2009) 10 SCC 84 — six factors for amendment (whether necessary for real controversy, whether bona fide, prejudice, no costs cure, fundamental change in nature of suit, delay).
Cite Rajesh Kumar Aggarwal v. K.K. Modi (2006) 4 SCC 385 — amendment to introduce new cause of action vs. clarify existing.
Cite Pankaja v. Yellappa (2004) 6 SCC 415 — amendment introducing time-barred claim not allowed unless relation-back doctrine applies.
Para 1: Reference to main suit, parties, stage.
Para 2: Pleading sought to be amended (plaint / WS / replication) and paragraph numbers.
Para 3: Stage of suit — critical. If issues framed but evidence not commenced — pre-trial. If evidence commenced — proviso engaged.
Para 4: Proposed amendments — annex marked-up copy in Annexure-A with insertions in underlined and deletions in strikethrough.
Para 5: Necessity — amendment is necessary to determine real question in controversy; without amendment, true issue cannot be adjudicated.
Para 6: When facts came to applicant's knowledge — establishes diligence timeline.

Para 7 (if trial commenced): Due diligence — specific narration showing that despite reasonable diligence, the amendment could not have been raised before commencement of trial. Examples: subsequent events, fresh documents discovered, new development of law, party's own evolved understanding ruled out unless backed by fresh discovery.
Para 8: No prejudice to opposite party that cannot be compensated by costs; amendment does not displace settled rights or destroy admissions made.
Para 9: No change in nature / character of suit. No new cause of action introduced that is time-barred.
Para 10: Limitation — if amendment introduces new claim, check if claim is within limitation OR if relation-back to original plaint is available (only in narrow circumstances).

Common permissible amendments: typographical / clerical corrections, clarification of existing pleas, adding alternative reliefs, particulars of fraud / misrepresentation, change of valuation, addition/deletion of parties (technically O.1 R.10 — but mention).

Common impermissible amendments: introducing entirely new cause of action especially time-barred; withdrawal of admissions; introducing inconsistent / contradictory pleas; changing nature of suit (e.g., possession suit to title suit fundamentally).
Cite Heeralal v. Kalyan Mal (1998) 1 SCC 278 — withdrawal of admissions ordinarily not permitted.
Cite Ragu Thilak D. John v. S. Rayappan (2001) 2 SCC 472 — amendment to introduce relief of declaration not allowed if substantive suit different.
Cite Sampath Kumar v. Ayyakannu (2002) 7 SCC 559 — amendment to alter relief from injunction to declaration permitted in appropriate cases.
For commercial courts: Order XI proceeding rules of Commercial Courts Act override certain CPC defaults; amendments more restricted.
Affidavit in support is mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.
